data.description: So... Why Isn't the AI Bubble Popping?  In 2025, OpenAI lost about $1.60 for every $1 it earned just running its business. Yet Big Tech is still on track to spend around $725 billion on AI infrastructure this year alone, and just seven tech giants now make up about a third of the S&P 500, the same index sitting in millions of Americans’ retirement accounts. The risk is already enormous, and we've yet to account for both Anthropic and OpenAI's upcoming IPOs - meaning 2027... could get very, VERY volatile.  On this Episode, We’ll Cover:  - Why Nvidia, Big Tech and the White House are all-in on the AI boom  - How Nvidia became the shovel seller of the AI gold rush  - OpenAI’s losses and the circular financing loop between Nvidia, OpenAI and Oracle  - Why AI IPOs like Anthropic and OpenAI shift the risk onto retail investors  - What South Korea’s KOSPI crash reveals about AI concentration in the S&P 500  ----  Support Our Work: https://www.youtube.com/@MonkeyExplains1999/membership  ----  Sauce - https://pastebin.com/JJyM2DuD  ----  AI Disclosure: I want to be clear about how we create our videos. We're a small team of actual people and all of the visuals you see are hand-drawn.  AI is used ONLY for Dubbing/Narration. Most of the team, including myself are based in South East Asia and English isn't our best language. I personally had negative experiences being bullied for my Singaporean Accent when I worked in the marketing industry. And now, considering the subjects of our videos - this is a way to help protect the identity of everyone working on this channel.  Everything from scripting, jokes, references, editing, and overall creativity, is 100% me and my amazing team of animators and illustrators. data.description: Paul Stamets is widely regarded as the father of modern applied mycology for his work on fungi and their applications in human health. data.description: George Osborne was UK Chancellor of the Exchequer from 2010 to 2016, taking on the role at just 38. Since leaving politics he has built a remarkable second act: editor of the Evening Standard, partner at Robey Warshaw, chair of the British Museum, and today Managing Director and Head of Countries at OpenAI, alongside roles at Coinbase and the Political Currency podcast with Ed Balls. In this episode, George talks to Wilf about why he believes the AI revolution is deeply deflationary, whether the UK and Europe are being left behind by America's tech boom, and the significance of big tech companies now wielding budgets to rival governments.  He explains why he doesn’t think  the mid-terms mark a sea change in the AI data centre build out, claiming OpenAI had already changed its approach to engage with local communities in a positive way. He also explains how the increasing desire internationally that data be housed “in-country” is creating plenty of opportunity for OpenAI’s data expansion outside the US. George then reflects on his time in Number 11 – the case for austerity, why a mandate matters, and the failure of the Remain campaign in the Brexit referendum   – and gives his take on the potential for the UK rejoining the EU. He also explains why he thinks the Conservative Party should be open to a warmer relationship with the EU, but why he’d never vote for Labour even if it provided a route to overturn Brexit. George and Wilf discuss the track record of the Bank Of England and other central banks in recent years - as inflation has persisted and many have deviated from their mandates -  including George’s support for Kevin Warsh at the Fed for the changes he’s attempting to bring about.   Recorded Tuesday 10th November 2026   Watch George on the Political Currency podcast here - https://www.youtube.com/@polcurrency   Watch the full episode on The Master Investor Podcast YouTube channel   Follow @WilfredFrost on X and Linked In    And NEW: Subscribe to The Master Investor Podcast Memos    Sponsored by BNY Investments, Interactive Brokers - ibkr.com/masterinvestor, The World Gold Council and London Stock Exchange Group (LSEG).    The Master Investor Podcast is produced by Paradine Productions, Master Investor Ltd in association with Bird Lime Media.   This podcast is for information purposes only. data.description: View the Show Notes Page for This EpisodeBecome a Member to Receive Exclusive ContentSign Up to Receive Peter’s Weekly NewsletterView our full terms of useIn this episode, Peter welcomes back Nav Chandel, a distinguished professor and world-renowned expert in mitochondrial biology, for a conversation that challenges many conventional assumptions about mitochondria and their role in health and aging. Nav begins by explaining what mitochondria do beyond ATP production, emphasizing their critical role in cellular communication and signaling. He explores how mitochondria communicate through hydrogen peroxide, metabolites, and mitochondrial DNA and RNA, and how these signals influence inflammation, immune function, and epigenetic regulation. The conversation then turns to the relationship between mitochondrial dysfunction and aging, including what the term “mitochondrial dysfunction” actually means and why it is often misused. Drawing on his own research, Nav takes a deep dive into metformin, explaining its effects on mitochondrial function, metabolism, and inflammation. He examines the evidence for its potential benefits in preventing age-related diseases and why findings from cancer trials have been disappointing. data.description: Paul Christiano is head of the Alignment Research Center. Previously, he was head of AI safety at the US AI Safety Institute. Before that, he led alignment at OpenAI, where he invented RLHF. He’s recently joined OpenAI’s board (though here he is speaking as a private citizen).Paul thinks that on the current trajectory (absent any slowing down), there is a 1 in 3 chance that we could have superintelligence powerful enough to overthrow the government within a year. (He articulates a concrete scenario).He argues that the labs should pause further algorithmic progress until they can secure their weights and research secrets. Otherwise China could simply steal the superintelligence in the middle of the intelligence explosion, and the labs would no longer be able to slow down even if they saw their models going off the rails.He also explains how AIs will be trained during the intelligence explosion, and why even a system trained entirely inside a data center could still have the capabilities profile such that humans would have very little chance of competing with it or controlling it.And he discusses the plan for alignment - basically, making a superintelligence that actually does what we ask the way we mean it. Fixing reward hacks and building better graders will help up till the next few model generations, but he thinks that no single current approach has better than even odds of letting us control superintelligence. The hope is that the AIs figure out the solution to this problem during the intelligence explosion.Watch on YouTube; read the transcript.Sponsors* Jane Street has finally come around on formal methods. Ron Minsky, who co-heads Jane Street’s technology group, told me that up until recently, formal methods just weren’t worth the cost. But coding agents have made them easier to apply AND increased the importance of code verification. So now Jane Street is hiring Formal Methods Engineers in both their London and New York offices. If you’re interested, or if you want to watch my full conversation with Ron, go to janestreet.com/dwarkesh* Antithesis is NOT another LLM-based code-review tool. It doesn’t try to reason abstractly about how a PR might break your system. Instead, it just runs your code. You start by defining the rules that your system must never break. Then, whenever an agent proposes a change, Antithesis runs your code through thousands of adversarial worlds, testing whether or not it still adheres to your rules. If you want to try it, go to antithesis.com/dwarkesh and use code DWARKESH for 50% off your first month.* WorkOS lets you give agents their own sign-up flow. This matters because agents tend to pick tools they can use right away, rather than ones that require humans to register. Fortunately, providing this kind of dedicated path is easy: if you already use WorkOS for login, you just toggle on “Agent Registration” in the WorkOS dashboard. Once it’s enabled, you can decide what agents are allowed to do on their own, and what needs to wait until the person they’re working for gets involved, all with the permissions you’ve already set up.
